title: Pirates, Giants dismantle aces, combine for 35 hits in potential game of season
content:
In what was supposed to be a battle of aces between the Pittsburgh Pirates and San Francisco Giants, it was the bats that took center stage, as the clubs combined for 35 hits in a 13-12 walk-off win for Pittsburgh.

For San Francisco, a comeback of epic proportions — the club was down 11-5 entering the fourth inning — was for naught.

Paul Skenes, last year’s NL Cy Young Award winner, lasted all of 4 2/3 innings, having surrendered five runs on eight hits. His counterpart, Logan Webb, a perennial All-Star, found himself chased in the second inning, with nine runs on nine hits being charged to his line. Skenes, who entered with a 3.79 ERA, exited with a 3.97 mark, and Webb, a 3.72 ERA holder, saw his season mark skyrocket to 4.21, his highest since becoming a full-time starter in 2021.

With both aces effectively nonfactors, it was a showcase for hitting. Despite the 25 combined runs, only two home runs were hit, one each by the Giants and Pirates. And in the end, it wasn’t another base knock that won Pittsburgh the game. Rather, a throwing error by third baseman Osleivis Basabe allowed Brandon Lowe to scamper home for the winner.
